sub_questions.question: Will an edited knowledge base document update on its own?
Does the Team plan include a dedicated customer success manager?

claims.claim: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed automatically through parse, enrich, chunk, and re-index.
claims.guide_evidence: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed through these same four stages before its chunks are available for retrieval again

claims.claim: The document isn't searchable until re-processing finishes.
claims.guide_evidence: a newly indexed document is not searchable mid-processing.

claims.claim: Team workspaces get a dedicated customer success manager.
claims.guide_evidence: Enterprise is a separately sold, typically self-hosted or VPC-deployed product line for organizations that need capabilities beyond what any Cloud tier offers, such as single sign-on, detailed audit logging, and a dedicated customer success manager

claims.claim: The customer success manager will reach out after the customer upgrades.

customer_safety_issues: Tells the customer that Team includes a dedicated customer success manager, which the guide attributes to Enterprise. The customer could act on this when choosing a plan.
evaluation.rationale: The document re-processing answer is accurate and grounded. The answer wrongly says Team includes a dedicated customer success manager, but the guide lists that as an Enterprise capability beyond any Cloud tier. It also invents an outreach after upgrade, so a customer could buy the wrong plan.
